note: AWK-57's transcription of the two dated Brooklyn Symphony Orchestra Mexico
tour Concerts, separated from the script that applies it. Read by
transcribe_programs.py --plan, asserted by mexico-tour-programs.test.ts.
DECIDED AND NEVER REGENERATED, in the sense period-and-forms.json uses and
both program declarations repeat. The sources are two public web pages and
a public RSS feed rather than a scan -- so unlike AWK-64 and AWK-82 they
CAN be re-read -- but nothing in this repository derives this file from
them, there is no parser to run, and the spreadsheet holds no row for
either date. A correction here is the only record of the correction.
THIS TICKET SAT BLOCKED FOR A WEEK ON ONE FACT. AWK-57 was split out of
AWK-38 on 2026-08-29 as the item blocked on 'a fact no source in this repo
holds' -- the tour date. ADR-0012 reached the same conclusion by
inspection. Alex supplied two links on 2026-09-06 and both dates, both
halls and the conductor came out of them at once.
FOUR THINGS THE TICKET AND ADR-0012 BELIEVED DID NOT SURVIVE THE SOURCES,
and they are recorded here rather than only in the ticket because this file
is what a later reader will find first:
1. The tour did NOT repeat the 2020-02-23 Brooklyn Museum program.
Brooklyn played five works; the tour played four. Danzon No. 4 and the
Kempton Ricercar were not on tour, and Huapango -- which Brooklyn did
not play -- was.
2. So the tour Concerts do NOT share `pi-20200223-*`, which is what both
the ticket and ADR-0012 called for. `order` lives on the Program item,
so a shared item would carry Brooklyn's ordering into a Concert where
the work sits elsewhere -- Mozartiana is third at the museum and
second on tour. The two tour dates are a run WITH EACH OTHER and share
nothing with Brooklyn. `cnc-20200223` is not touched.
3. The encore was NOT a work the printed program lacked. ADR-0012's
'Encores need nothing new' reasons from Huapango being absent from the
program; both source pages print it third of four. Alex resolved the
apparent conflict from memory on 2026-09-06: it was programmed and
then REPEATED as the encore. Hence two Huapango items per Concert.
ADR-0012's conclusion survives -- an encore is a Program item with a
high order and a note, and needs no schema change -- but its premise
does not.
4. `attended` cannot come from seed_participation.py, which the ticket's
step 4 required. That plan is generated from the participation
checklist AND bso-graph.json; the graph holds no row for either date
and never will, because the spreadsheet holds none. `attended` is
declared here, as AWK-64 and AWK-82 declare it.
THE GRAPH'S IDS ARE NOT THE SPACE'S IDS, and this file was first drafted
with three that do not exist in Contentful: `orc-bso`,
`cmp-van-beethoven-ludwig` and `cnd-nicholas-armstrong`. All three are
bso-graph.json ids. The space holds the Brooklyn Symphony Orchestra under
`7GW6fT7mUQE6pZLJXHj1TC` and Beethoven under `2tfdUTvmRn1etYq5czTknE`,
because 33 hand-curated concerts and their links live under Contentful
auto-ids -- participation.json's note says the same of its own join key.
Every id in `reuse` below was read back from the Delivery API on
2026-09-06, and verify_reuse re-reads them at apply time.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT FINISH is the thing AWK-57 was opened for: attaching the
three BSO Mexico 2020 recordings. See `pendingRecordings`.
TWO PRIMARY PAGES AND ONE CORROBORATING FEED, and the distinction matters
because the feed is what everyone had already read.
The two pages are a performer's own concert log -- Andrew Westling, a BSO
player -- one page per date, each giving the date, the start time, the
hall, the city, the orchestra, the conductor and the program in order.
They are third-party and self-published, which is the honest description;
they are also the only source anywhere that dates these concerts, and the
conductor and program they give are independently corroborated below.
The feed is the channel RSS that docs/archive/recording-curation.md was
built from, and it returns the 15 most recent uploads and no more. Its
three 'BSO Mexico 2020' entries carry a description the curation pass did
not quote: 'Brooklyn Symphony Orchestra - MEXICO TOUR 2020 / Felipe
Tristan, Associate Conductor / February-March 2020', then a list of
participating institutions, then the program. That is where the conductor
corroboration comes from, and where the word Encore is explicit rather
than only in a video title.
THE FEED NAMES THREE INSTITUTIONS AND ONLY ONE IS BELOW. Escuela Superior
de Musica y Danza de Monterrey, Conservatorio Nacional de Musica, and
Escuela Superior de Musica de Mexico. The Conservatorio is the 2020-02-29
venue; Monterrey is a different city. So the tour had dates beyond these
two, in at least two cities, and nothing here dates them or gives their
programs. They are not created -- absence of evidence, not evidence of
absence, and a Concert with no date is not a Concert this archive can
hold.
Live entry ids this transcription links but does not create. Every one
was read back from the Delivery API on 2026-09-06 before it was written
down, and the display value beside each id is what came back.
NOTHING IS CREATED EXCEPT HALLS. No Work, no Composer, no Conductor, no
Orchestra, no Season -- the entire tour program was already in the
archive, played at other times by other forces. That is the exact
opposite of AWK-82, where all seven program lines were new works, and it
is why this declaration has no `works`, `composers`, `conductors` or
`orchestras` section at all rather than empty ones.
THE NAMES BESIDE THE IDS ARE A CHECK, NOT A LABEL. transcribe_programs.py
re-reads each entry and aborts if the id has gone missing, if it now
resolves to a different content type, or if its live display value no
longer matches what is recorded here. So correcting a name here is not
tidying; it is the thing that keeps the check honest.
TWO IDS ARE CONTENTFUL AUTO-IDS and that is not a mistake to tidy up.
`7GW6fT7mUQE6pZLJXHj1TC` and `2tfdUTvmRn1etYq5czTknE` are the live
Brooklyn Symphony Orchestra and Beethoven. The readable `orc-bso` and
`cmp-van-beethoven-ludwig` exist in bso-graph.json and nowhere else; a
link to either would be accepted by Contentful and render a Concert with
a hole in it. See the top note.
THE FOUR WORKS ARE THE POINT OF REUSING RATHER THAN CREATING. Every one
carries slugs, forms and a composer link the archive already settled, and
two of them -- Leonore and Mozartiana -- are the works the two mapped
recordings will eventually hang from.

leonore.title: Leonore Overture No. 3
leonore.why: Beethoven's, live slug `leonore-overture-no-3`, forms [Overture]. Also `pi-20200223-1` at the Brooklyn Museum six days earlier, which is the one work whose position is the same on both programs.

mozartiana.title: Suite No. 4 in G Major ("Mozartiana")
mozartiana.why: Tchaikovsky's, nickname `Mozartiana`, forms [Suite]. The entry id keeps the importer's truncated hash form; the live slug is the clean `suite-no-4-in-g-major-mozartiana`. Curation video #14 maps here.

huapango.title: Huapango
huapango.why: Moncayo's, and the trap ADR-0012 names. The archive's only prior Huapango PROGRAM ITEM is `pi-20001216-2`, on a pre-tenure 2000 concert two decades from the recording -- a title matcher lands there confidently. The WORK is what is reused; that item is not touched. Two items below link this one Work.

lesPreludes.title: Les Preludes (d'apres Lamartine)
lesPreludes.why: Liszt's. The archive spells it without diacritics and this follows the space rather than the sources, which print `Les Preludes` and `Les Préludes` respectively. Curation video #8 maps here.

beethoven.why: A Contentful auto-id, NOT `cmp-van-beethoven-ludwig`, which exists only in the parser graph. Confirmed by reading the composer link off the live Leonore work rather than by guessing at a readable id.

moncayo.why: Filed under the doubled surname, unaccented, and with no period set. AWK-37's diacritics pass did not reach him; leaving that as it is, because a composer's spelling is that ticket's business and changing it here would put a decided thing in two places.

tristan.name: Felipe Tristan
tristan.why: Already in the archive with 11 concerts, 2018 to 2026. Both source pages credit him and all three video descriptions call him Associate Conductor. NOT Nicholas Armstrong, who conducted the Brooklyn Museum date six days earlier -- the differing conductor is a second reason these are separate Concerts rather than one program repeated. `conductor` has no `name` field; the value here is the firstName/lastName join verify_reuse compares against.

bso.name: Brooklyn Symphony Orchestra
bso.why: A Contentful auto-id, NOT `orc-bso`. Read off the live `cnc-20200223`, which links this same entry. Its abbreviation is `BSO`, which is what the concerts table renders and what an invariant message names instead of an id.

s47.label: BSO Season 47, 2019-2020
s47.why: The season the Brooklyn Museum date already belongs to, and its live notes read `SUSPENDED; 2020-2021 SEASON CANCELED, DUE TO COVID-19 PANDEMIC` -- these two concerts are within a fortnight of that. ADR-0006 lets a FESTIVAL concert carry no season and AWK-82 made the field optional; a tour date is not that. This is the orchestra's own numbered season, played abroad.

note: THE ARCHIVE'S FIRST HALLS OUTSIDE THE UNITED STATES. docs/agents/facts.md
records 'all 13 halls are Brooklyn/NYC, so the archive holds no tour venue
at all' as the general form of this ticket's problem; the space now holds
18 and the statement was still true of every one of them until these two.
`location` follows the space's format -- `Town, NY` for the Brooklyn and
New York halls, `Institution, Town, NY` where the hall sits inside a
larger campus -- with the country added, which no existing location
carries because none needed it. The Auditorio takes the long form because
it is a room inside the Conservatorio; the Castillo does not.
SLUGS ARE HAND-WRITTEN and folded the way ADR-0008 folds a filing name.
Diacritics fold out of a slug and stay in the name: `Musica` in the slug
would be wrong twice over, since the slug does not contain the
institution at all. hall.slug is read by no route today and is still
swept by AWK-61's whitespace invariant.
THE ACCENTS IN `location` ARE DELIBERATE, and they are the one place this
declaration does not follow the space's existing spelling. The archive
writes `Les Preludes` and `Moncayo Garcia` unaccented because the
spreadsheet did and AWK-37's pass has not reached them; these two halls
are new records with no such history, and writing `Musica` to match the
neighbours would be inventing a wrong spelling rather than preserving one.

hal-auditorio-silvestre-revueltas.name: Auditorio Silvestre Revueltas
hal-auditorio-silvestre-revueltas.location: Conservatorio Nacional de Música, Mexico City, Mexico
hal-auditorio-silvestre-revueltas.why: The 2020-02-29 venue, printed by the source as `Auditorio Silvestre Revueltas, Conservatorio Nacional de Musica`. Split into name and location per the space's format. The Conservatorio is one of the three institutions the video descriptions name, which is the only overlap between the two source kinds.

hal-castillo-de-chapultepec.name: Castillo de Chapultepec
hal-castillo-de-chapultepec.why: The 2020-03-01 venue. A castle and museum rather than a concert hall, which is unremarkable for a touring afternoon program and worth one line so nobody later reads it as a transcription slip.

note: Ids and titles follow AWK-59, AWK-64 and AWK-82: cnc-YYYYMMDD and a title
of 'YYYY-MM-DD — <institution>' with an em dash.
ITEM IDS DERIVE FROM THE FIRST NIGHT AND BOTH CONCERTS CARRY THE SAME
FIVE. This is the archive's run shape and the first time a committed
declaration has used it -- AWK-64 and AWK-82 both create items fresh per
Concert, because their Concerts are unrelated. Nine runs already live in
the space work exactly this way: cnc-20070523 links pi-20070520-*, and
archive-corrections.test.ts asserts the same of the 2008-12-13/14 pair.
THE APPLIER HAD TO LEARN THIS. transcribe_programs.py builds each
Concert's program from the items declared inline on it, so five items
across two Concerts produced ten plan rows and a guard count that would
have had to say ten where five entities exist. AWK-57 added a dedupe by
entry id, in the same spirit as AWK-82 making `season` optional: the
first declaration to need a shape is the one that pays for it.
SHARED WITH EACH OTHER, NEVER WITH THE BROOKLYN MUSEUM. Sharing
`pi-20200223-*` is what AWK-57's body and ADR-0012 both called for and it
is wrong -- see the top note. Worth knowing: the 7-day span to 2020-02-23
is inside app/lib/invariants.ts's 14-day ceiling, so the build would have
accepted it. No rule reads whether two Concerts played the same program,
which is exactly why that argument had to be made in prose.
attended is true on both and satOut is empty on both: Alex played both
dates in full, stated 2026-09-06.
`sourceNote` IS NOT WRITTEN TO CONTENTFUL, following AWK-82. The content
model has nowhere to put a start time or a tour's name, and concert.
dateNote qualifies a DATE rather than describing an occasion -- filling it
with 'Mexico tour' would be a third use of a field whose twelve live
values are all either a fuzzy date or the second-night sentence below.
What says Mexico on the rendered page is the hall's location.

cnc-20200229.title: 2020-02-29 — BSO
cnc-20200229.sourceNote: Saturday 7:00 PM, Auditorio Silvestre Revueltas at the Conservatorio Nacional de Música, Mexico City. The first of the two dated tour concerts, and a leap day.

program.label: Leonore Overture No. 3
program.why: Printed as `Leonore Overture No. 3, Op. 72b`. The label follows the archive's existing title for this Work rather than the printed opus number, because the Work record is reused and a per-performance label that adds an opus the Work does not carry would read as a different Work.

program.label: Suite No. 4 in G Major ("Mozartiana")
program.why: SECOND on tour, THIRD at the Brooklyn Museum. This one item is the clearest reason the two programs cannot share Program items: `order` lives here, and `pi-20200223-3` carries a 3.

program.label: Huapango
program.why: Programmed, third of four, on both source pages. Brooklyn did not play it. ADR-0012 assumed the encore was a work the printed program lacked; this item is the half of that assumption the sources overturn.

program.label: Les Preludes (d'apres Lamartine)
program.why: Printed as `Les Preludes`. Label follows the archive's fuller existing title, which names the Lamartine after which Liszt titled it.

program.label: Huapango
program.why: THE SAME WORK AGAIN. Alex stated on 2026-09-06 that Huapango was repeated as the encore, which reconciles the source pages printing it in the program against the video titled `MONCAYO Haupango Encore` and described as `Program: *Encore* MONCAYO Huapango`. The video's spelling of the title is a typo; its description spells it correctly, as does the archive. ADR-0012 asks for `a high order and note: "Encore"`; with five items, 5 is the high order and also its true position, so nothing has to be invented.

cnc-20200301.title: 2020-03-01 — BSO
cnc-20200301.sourceNote: Sunday 1:00 PM, Castillo de Chapultepec, Mexico City. The second of the two dated tour concerts, the next day.

program.label: Leonore Overture No. 3
program.why: The same five items as 2020-02-29, repeated verbatim. They are declared twice because transcribe_programs.py reads each Concert's program from the items on it; the applier dedupes by entry id, and mexico-tour-programs.test.ts asserts the two lists are deep-equal so an edit to one copy cannot drift from the other.

note: THE THREE VIDEOS THIS DECLARATION DOES NOT ATTACH, and the reason AWK-57
is not finished by applying it. Not written to Contentful; the `recording`
entries would be a separate pass and transcribe_programs.py has no
section for them.
WHAT IS STILL MISSING IS WHICH DATE. The descriptions say only
'February-March 2020' and name three participating institutions across at
least two cities, so there were tour dates beyond these two. Both
Concerts below share one program, so app/lib/invariants.ts's
`recording-item-on-concert-program` is satisfied by EITHER Concert and
cannot catch a wrong choice -- the check that would normally backstop a
guess is blind here, which is the whole argument for not guessing.
THE ITEM IS KNOWN EVEN THOUGH THE CONCERT IS NOT, and that asymmetry is
why these are worth recording now. Each video names its work; the work
resolves to exactly one item on the shared program. Only `recording.
concert` is undetermined.
THE IDS ARE HERE SO NOBODY RE-DERIVES THEM. The channel feed returns the
15 most recent uploads and no more -- these three are from 2021-04 and
already sit at positions 8, 10 and 14. They will fall off.
docs/archive/recording-curation.md is the worksheet for the other twelve
and ADR-0012 forbids scripting any of it.

mozartiana.title: BSO Mexico 2020 - TCHAIKOVSKY Orchestral Suite No. 4, Op. 61 ("Mozartiana")
mozartiana.why: Curation #14. Its description lists all four movements with timings, which is the only per-video detail in the batch that could not have come from the program alone.

huapangoEncore.title: BSO Mexico 2020 - MONCAYO Haupango Encore
huapangoEncore.why: Curation #10, and the one video that identifies its own Program item unambiguously -- it is the encore, so it is item 5 rather than item 3, and the two are the same Work. `Haupango` in the title is the video's typo; the description spells it correctly.

note: Counts the test asserts, so a hand edit that drops or doubles something
fails rather than applying quietly. transcribe_programs.py checks the
same numbers against the plan it builds and exits before touching the
network if they disagree.
`programItems` IS 5, NOT 10. Both Concerts declare the same five items,
so the raw plan holds ten rows; the applier dedupes by entry id before
comparing. This number is what would catch that dedupe being removed.
THE SIX ZEROES ARE FINDINGS. Nothing is created but Halls -- every Work,
Composer, Conductor and Orchestra the tour needs was already in the
archive. AWK-82's guards are the mirror image, with seven works created
and none reused.
`entriesCreated` is the sum of every creation: 2 halls, 5 program items
and 2 concerts. The three pendingRecordings are NOT entries and are not
counted.
